sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Our Freiburg data is recent, so there is no city trend yet; the figures below are for weekdays in August and September 2026, during the university's summer break.

Freiburg has made parking a political topic mainly through residents' permits and street prices. A council majority backed a sharp rise in permit fees in 2021, after 28 years at €30 a year, and approved extending resident parking to Herdern and Oberau [0]. The resulting fee ordinance of December 2021 was struck down by the Federal Administrative Court in June 2023, which accepted a €360 base fee but not the unequal treatment between price bands [1]. The city then set a flat €200 a year from December 2023 [2]. The street is the dear option: since February 2026 street parking costs €4.20 an hour in the central zone, with a flat 24-hour rate of €21 across large parts of it [4]. The city's garages are cheaper, at €2.20–2.70 an hour, and the city kept their prices unchanged [4]. Looking ahead, the city is studying how the Dreisam area could look if a planned Stadttunnel is built, which Autobahn GmbH expects to take 60–80% of today's traffic there [3].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The city's garage company, Freiburger Kommunalbauten (FKB), part of the Freiburger Stadtbau group, manages about 3,200 spaces in its own and managed garages [6]. In 2025 it closed the Rotteckgarage in stages for renovation, sending drivers to the Konzerthaus and Schlossberg garages [5]. The garage has four charging stations [7]. A transport campaign group criticised a plan to spend €9.5 million on the Bahnhofsgarage [11]. Ticketless entry by number plate is coming to FKB's garages too: in 2023 evopark announced that the Schlossberg and Rotteck garages would soon be connected to its platform [9].

Public charging is mostly outside garages: about 540 points in 2025, with a target of more than 1,500 by 2030 [8]. Tourism is strong, with a record 2.12 million overnight stays in 2023 [12], and Galeria took ownership of its building at Bertoldsbrunnen in 2025 [13].

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
Freiburg's garages are split between the city, private operators and the transport company. FKB's three central garages (Rotteck, Schlossberg and Gerhart-Graf-Halle) charge €2.70 an hour and about €34 a day, 12% above their neighbours, and run at 37% on weekdays. Contipark's three garages charge the same and average 42%, and APCOA's two, a little cheaper, 34%.

Price does not decide use. The busiest garage we measure is Contipark's Zähringer Tor (62%), which charges €1.50 an hour, the cheapest in the centre. Among the others, the small Gerhart-Graf-Halle (45%) and Schwarzwald City (40%) do best. The five garages run by the transport company at the edge of the city charge €8 a day and average 26%, and the 750-space Westarkaden, also at €1.50 an hour with a €6 day ticket, is the emptiest we measure (14%). Garages within 500 m of the Münsterplatz average 38%, and those more than 2 km out about 21%. Weekends are quieter, 23% against 29% on weekdays, and the Landratsamt car park, which serves a district office, falls from 29% to 8%.
